It is owned by China Nonferrous Metal Mining (Group) (55%), Hong Kong Zhongfei Mining Investment (30%) and NFC Africa Mining (15%), has yearly capacity of 8,000 tonnes of copper cathode and 4,000 tonnes of copper concentrate, and employs 426 Zambian and Chinese staff.

Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production.desc: Shell's deep-water oil and gas producer in the Gulf of Guinea, one of four businesses wholly owned by Shell plc that make up the Shell companies in Nigeria, and the operator of the Bonga FPSO. It holds 55% of OML 118 and 55% of OML 135, both Shell-operated, and 43.75% of the Esso-operated OML 133; its interest in OPL 245 ended when the licence expired in 2021. Shell's two Nigerian producers together put out 367,683 barrels of oil equivalent a day in 2022, and SNEPCo paid US$907 million in Nigerian corporate taxes and royalties that year.

SOCO International plc.desc: An international oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in London and listed on the London Stock Exchange, whose shareholders approved a change of registered name to Pharos Energy plc on 16 October 2019, expected to take effect the same day. Wildlife Alliance.desc: A conservation organisation registered as a 501(c)(3) non-profit, whose IRS filings give New York, NY, and whose own site gives a contact address in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It was founded in 1995 as the Global Survival Network and renamed Wildlife Alliance in 2006; its work has included anti-poaching patrols in the Russian Far East from 1995, help for turtle protection in India from 1996, biodiversity work in Myanmar and Thailand, support for expanding the Galápagos Marine Reserve in Ecuador from 1998, and reforestation in Cambodia's Cardamom Mountains from 2008. It reported revenue of US$9,233,046 against expenses of US$11,762,384 for the year to December 2024.
